newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank, insurers up on auto rate report.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank, insurers up on auto rate report.

text.p: UK insurance stocks were buoyant on Monday following a report in the Sunday Times that car insurance rates are set to soar, traders said.
The report said a quarterly survey of premiums indicated that rates had already climbed by an average of eight percent in the past three months and were set to rise by 25 percent before Christmas.
Shares in Royal Bank of Scotland, which owns Britain's largest car insurer, Direct Line, rose 4.5p to 485p by 0925 GMT and General Accident shares rose 8p to 654.5p.
Commercial Union was up 8p at 596-1/2 and Royal Sun Alliance was up 1-1/2p at 404.

"There is talk of car insurance rates going up and the Royal Bank of Scotland and others are up on the back of that," said one trader, adding that the anecdotal evidence still seemed to indicate that rates remained relatively soft.
Another said, "I suppose it's inevitable rates will go up at some point but at the moment the market is so competitive, if one company puts rates up it will lose the business to someone else."
Three of the companies surveyed, General Accident, Touchline and Dial Direct, have already increased some of their rates by more than 12 percent, the Sunday Times report said.

It said insurers were blaming a change in legislation for the increases. Updated actuarial tables will require insurers to pay out more for claims than previously thought, forcing insurers to increase premiums.
